The Complete Guide to Claude Plugins (10x your productivity)
Claude plugins will change how you use Claude forever, and I haven't seen anyone talk about how powerful they are.
Plugins unlock your Claude in ways you didn't know were possible, and in today's article, I'm giving you the ultimate guide to Claude plugins.
This is the closest thing you'll get to hiring a full-time role with Claude that knows exactly how you work and how you operate.
I'll cover:
What plugins are, how to use them, where to find valuable plugins, and most importantly, how to actually use Claude plugins for maximum productivity.
Let's dive right in.

What Even are Claude Plugins?

Before we get into how to use plugins, I have to make an important clarification.
Claude has three ways to extend its capabilities, and they all sound similar but do different things:
Connectors connect Claude to external services you already use (Gmail, Calendar, etc.).
Skills are saved reusable workflows.
Plugins go one level further and combine both Connectors + Skills into a single "role."
Where a skill is a single capability and a connector is an external service, a plugin can include several of each.
In short, think of a plugin as a complete workflow package rather than a single workflow.
Where to find them
You can access plugins in the Claude desktop app.
Claude desktop → Cowork → Customize → Plugins
Where to access plugins
The cool thing is, Anthropic already has 24+ plugins ready to use now across legal, marketing, productivity, and more departments.
Later in this article, I'll show you how to find other valuable plugins too!

Installing & Using Plugins

You have two methods for installing Claude plugins:
  1. Marketplace
This is where 99% of people should familiarize themselves with Plugins.
Following the steps displayed above, you'll be able to search and access the official Anthropic plugin marketplace.
This is where you'll find 28 plugins built by Anthropic across Design, Finance, Marketing, Engineering & more:
Marketplace
2. Create from scratch
Your other option is to create/upload a plugin from scratch.
In the "Customize" menu of Claude Cowork, you can select "+" which allows you to either:
a) Upload a plug-in from an external source
b) Create a plugin with Claude
Create plugin from scratch
To create your own plugin, you can simply prompt Cowork on what you want to build:
Prompting Claude to create a plugin
For method b, you can grab plugins built by someone else and install them (more on this later).
Prompting plugins
Prompting your plugins is also relatively easy.
Depending on the plugin and its exact role, you'll prompt it differently.
For example, below I installed the official marketing plugin by Anthropic, and a few sample prompts would be:
Analyze our competitors' positioning
Draft a blog post with SEO optimization
Plan a multi-channel campaign
Review content against our brand voice
Marketing plugin example prompts
When you send these prompts, Claude will tap into all your skills, MCPs, and context to create the best possible output.
A Simple Example Workflow
Here's what a connected Claude session looks like in practice for someone with Gmail, Google Calendar, and Notion connected:
PROMPT
"Read my emails from the last 24 hours, check my calendar for today, and give me a morning briefing. Flag anything urgent, summarise any important threads I need to respond to, and list my meetings with a one-line brief on each one. Then check my Notion workspace for any tasks tagged as high priority and add them to the briefing."
That single prompt pulls from three connected tools simultaneously, synthesises everything, and delivers a personalised morning briefing in under a minute.
You can also "customize" plugins directly inside of Claude to tweak existing plugins and workflow packages.
Customize plugins

Getting the Most Out of Your Plugins

I've been using Claude plugins since the release, and these are all the most valuable tips I could give you:
  • Let Claude audit your workflow before connecting anything - describe how you work and ask Claude which connectors/skills/MCPs to prioritise.
  • Take advantage of "Scheduled Tasks" - this allows you to run your plugins on a set schedule task (like a daily morning brief).
  • Use interactive connectors - Figma, Canva, Slack (these are extremely high leverage).
  • Use Notion connector - Notion is an awesome way to store data, and you can have an AI second brain database that your plugins automatically source information from!
  • Pair connectors with Claude Skills for fully automated workflows (aka build a skill that triggers a multi-connector workflow with a single slash command. Type /morning-brief and Claude pulls from Gmail, Calendar, and Notion automatically).
  • Import existing Skills - To create your first plugin, just import your existing Claude Skills and let Cowork build it.
  • Check the Anthropic connector directory regularly - Lastly, new connectors are being added constantly, and the ecosystem is growing fast.
